blocks.task_summary: Show that the Cartesian equation of plane P1 containing line L1 and point (2,1,5) is x + y - z = -2.
method_path: Find direction vector from given point to point on line
Compute normal vector via vector product of direction vectors
Substitute point into plane equation to find constant d
Write Cartesian equation x + y - z = -2
accepted_alternatives: Form parametric equations of plane using two vectors and point (0,0,2), eliminate parameters to obtain Cartesian equation.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: correct direction vector, e.g. (2,1,3)-(0,0,2)=(2,1,1) A1; attempt to find direction normal using vector product (M1); (2,1,1)×(1,0,1) = (1,1,-1) A1; correct substitution of a point on the line to obtain d A1; hence equation x+y-z=-2 AG

METHOD 2: attempt to form parametric equations of a plane through point (0,0,2) and two vectors (1,0,1) and (2,1,3) M1; r = (0,0,2)+λ(1,0,1)+μ(2,1,3) A1; x=λ+2μ, y=μ, z=2+λ+3μ; λ=x-2y; z=2+(x-2y)+3y => x+y-z=-2 AG

blocks.task_summary: Find b and d such that the three planes P1: x+y-z=-2, P2: 2x+by-z=3, P3: x-y+2z=d intersect in a line.
method_path: Form equations to eliminate one variable
Obtain condition for consistency (infinite solutions along line)
accepted_alternatives: Use row reduction to obtain condition for infinite solutions, leading to b=4/3, d=19.
Set determinant of coefficient matrix to zero to find b, then use consistency condition to find d.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to form an equation to eliminate one of the variables M1; (b-2)y+z=7 A1; 2y-3z=-2-d A1; (b-4/3)y = (d-19)/3 => b=4/3, d=19 A1
METHOD 2: attempt to use row reduction M1; matrix [1 1 -1 -2; 2 b -1 3; 1 -1 2 d] -> [1 1 -1 -2; 0 b-2 1 7; 0 -2 3 d+2] A1; further reduction yields condition (b-4/3)=0 and d=19 A1
METHOD 3: attempt to use determinant and equate it to zero (M1); det = 3b-4 = 0 => b=4/3 A1; then use determinant with constants to find d=19 A1
